elements.quote: We report interim results of a living systematic review.

elements.quote: We report interim results of a living systematic review. ... We identified a total of 30 studies that investigated VE against symptomatic and/ or asymptomatic infection. ... What is the efficacy/effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines in preventing asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections?

elements.quote: We considered studies of any design as long as they had a comparison group that investigated VE against SARS-CoV-2 infection and/or asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection after vaccination with an EMA-approved COVID-19 vaccine
elements.reason: The evidence specifies key inclusion criteria elements (comparison group, VE outcomes, EMA-approved vaccines), but does not provide explicit main inclusion and exclusion criteria as a complete set in the abstract.

elements.quote: For randomised controlled trials (RCTs), risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool-2 (RoB-2) [1]. To non-randomised studies, ROBINS-I was applied [2].
elements.reason: The abstract content specifies the risk-of-bias methods used.

elements.quote: Due to heterogeneity of study design, time point of analysis, vaccine used, population and settings, we did not perform a meta-analysis.

elements.reason: The abstract content provides the total number of included studies (30) and some characterization context is implied, but it does not clearly report total included participants or a consolidated summary of relevant study characteristics within the abstract evidence provided.

elements.quote: These interim results of a living systematic review show that after completed course the EMA-approved COVID-19 vaccines have a VE of 80% to 90% in preventing SARS-CoV2 infections, including asymptomatic ones.

elements.reason: The abstract content includes important limitations (e.g., publication landscape, preprints not fully captured).

elements.quote: Results of this living systematic review imply that COVID-19 vaccines are highly effective in preventing SARS-CoV-2 infections, including those which are asymptomatic. elements.quote: All vaccines approved by the European Medical Agency (EMA) at the time of writing demonstrated high vaccine efficacy/effectiveness (VE) against severe COVID-19. With vaccination programmes being implemented in most European countries, it becomes urgent to assess the extent to which these vaccines are also able to prevent symptomatic and asymptomatic infections to guide public health recommendations and develop strategies for fully vaccinated people.
elements.reason: Describes aspects of the current knowledge (high VE against severe COVID-19) and implies a gap/uncertainty (extent to which vaccines prevent symptomatic and asymptomatic infections), but does not explicitly detail important uncertainties beyond this.

elements.quote: With vaccination programmes being implemented in most European countries, it becomes urgent to assess the extent to which these vaccines are also able to prevent symptomatic and asymptomatic infections to guide public health recommendations and develop strategies for fully vaccinated people.
